title: Confirm Android SDK levels meet Play rules
statusNote: game/android/variables.gradle has targetSdk 36, compileSdk 36, minSdk 24, which meets the 31 Aug 2026 rule.
steps: Keep targetSdkVersion = 36 and compileSdkVersion = 36
Keep minSdkVersion = 24 (ads SDK 25.5+ needs 24)
Re-check each August when Google raises the target
feedback: New apps and updates must target API 36 since 31 Aug 2026.
The next bump (likely API 37, Aug 2027) is not announced yet.
doneMessage: The build already meets Play's API level rule, so no SDK bump stands between you and launch.

title: Wire UMP consent and ad frequency caps in the app
statusNote: game/src/platform/ads.js runs UMP consent before ads, shows Ad privacy choices, caps interstitials and makes rewarded opt-in.
steps: Consent form shown when UMP says it is required
Ads requested only when canRequestAds is true
Interstitial every 2 games, 3+ minutes apart, never at launch
Rewarded video only after the player taps Watch video
feedback: Messages still have to be created and published in AdMob (admob-privacy-messaging).
Keep interstitials at natural breaks; never show one on app open or exit.
doneMessage: Consent and ad pacing are in place; once AdMob messages are published the flow works end to end.

title: Decide personal vs organization Play account
statusNote: No store accounts exist yet and the developer is an individual without a registered company.
time: 15 min decision (D-U-N-S would add up to ~30 days)
steps: Pick Personal unless you already have an LLC
If Organization: get a free D-U-N-S number first
Decide which Google account will own everything
Turn on 2-Step Verification on that account
feedback: Personal accounts must pass the 12-tester / 14-day closed test.
Personal accounts show your legal name and country on Play.
Switching later means transferring the app to a new account.
doneMessage: With the account type chosen you can sign up for Play Console right away.

links.label: Required info to create an account

title: Get a physical Android 10+ phone for verification
statusNote: New personal accounts must verify with the Play Console app on a real phone; we don't know if you have one.
steps: Find a non-rooted Android phone on Android 10 or newer
Install the Google Play Console app
Keep it handy for testing ads, consent and gestures too
feedback: Emulators don't count for device verification.
The same phone may verify several accounts.
doneMessage: With a phone in hand you can finish Play Console verification and test real installs.

links.label: Verify access to an Android device

title: Host privacy policy, support email and website
statusNote: game/docs/PRIVACY.md is a template with blank name/email; listing.json has TODO support email and URL.
steps: Pick a host whose ROOT you control (user github.io, surge.sh, Firebase, own domain)
Give Claude your public name and support email
Claude builds privacy.html from PRIVACY.md and a small site
Publish it and note the URLs
Put email and URLs in store-launch/listing/listing.json
feedback: Policy must be a public HTML page, not a PDF, titled Privacy Policy.
Name the developer exactly as on the Play listing.
A project site (user.github.io/repo/) can't host app-ads.txt at the root.
doneMessage: Your policy URL and developer website are ready for Play App content and AdMob app-ads.txt.

title: Create Play Console account and verify identity
statusNote: No Play Console account exists yet.
steps: Go to play.google.com/console/signup and choose Personal
Enter developer name (e.g. Eddie G) and public developer email
Create or pick the Google payments profile (legal name, address)
Verify contact email and phone with the one-time codes
Pay the $25 fee with a card in your name
Upload your government ID when asked
Verify with the Play Console app on your Android phone
feedback: Legal name must match your ID and payments profile exactly.
Keep the contact email and phone working for the account's lifetime.
The fee is not refunded if verification fails on bad info.
doneMessage: Your developer account is live, so you can create the app and claim com.eddieg.aliensudoku.

title: Declare EU trader status (due 1 Feb 2027)
statusNote: Required of every Play account from Nov 2026 (reported); no account exists yet.
cost: Optional PO box / second phone line
time: 15 min (+ setting up a business address if wanted)
steps: Open Play Console > Account details > Declare status
Ad-funded app in the EU/UK: answer Trader
Enter and verify a public phone number and address
Or exclude EEA/UK countries if you won't disclose them
feedback: Trader details show to EU/UK users from 1 Mar 2027 (reported).
Choosing non-trader just to hide details risks suspension.
Could not verify on a Google page; follow the Console banner.
doneMessage: Trader status is settled, so updates won't be blocked and EU users can keep installing.

title: Create the app and claim the package name
statusNote: No Play Console app exists; com.eddieg.aliensudoku is not yet registered.
steps: Play Console > Create app
Name: Alien Sudoku; language English (US)
Type: Game; Free
Enter package name com.eddieg.aliensudoku if asked
Accept the policy and export law declarations
Check Android developer verification shows Registered
feedback: Creating the app auto-registers the package for developer verification.
A free app can never become paid later.
doneMessage: The package name is yours; you can now fill in App content while builds get sorted out.

title: Create and verify the AdMob account
statusNote: No AdMob account exists; the app uses Google's test ids.
time: 20 min + up to 24 h review (rarely 2 weeks)
steps: Sign in at admob.google.com with your long-term Google account
Choose Individual account type
Accept the AdMob terms
Enter payment details so the account can be verified
Wait for the approval email
feedback: One AdMob account per person; close any old one first.
Account type can't be changed later.
doneMessage: AdMob is approved, so you can create the real app id and ad units.

title: Add the Android app and three ad units in AdMob
statusNote: game/android/.../strings.xml and ads.js still use Google test ids.
steps: Apps > Add app > Android > Not listed on a store yet
Copy the app id (ca-app-pub-...~...)
Create units: Banner (adaptive), Interstitial, Rewarded
Rewarded: amount 1, item hint
Send Claude the app id, 3 unit ids and your pub- id
feedback: Ad unit ids aren't secret, but keep test and live builds separate.
New units can take up to an hour to serve.
doneMessage: Real ids are ready; Claude can wire them into the production build.

title: Publish GDPR and US state consent messages
statusNote: The app calls UMP, but no messages exist until you create them in AdMob.
steps: AdMob > Privacy & messaging > European regulations: create message
Add your privacy policy URL; choose Consent + Manage options
Pick the Android app; publish
Create a US states regulations message; publish
Test with UMP debug geography on your phone
feedback: Without a published GDPR message, EEA/UK users get no consent form and fewer ads.
The in-app Ad privacy choices button reopens these forms.
doneMessage: Consent is compliant in the EU, UK and regulated US states.

title: Set max ad content rating to PG or G
statusNote: No ad content rating is set in AdMob or in AdMob.initialize().
steps: AdMob > Blocking controls > Ad content rating
Choose PG (or G for maximum safety) for the app
Optionally block sensitive categories (dating, gambling)
feedback: Play requires ads to suit the app's content rating (likely 3+/7+).
G/PG also lowers risk given the cute art.
doneMessage: Ads will match a family-friendly rating, protecting your listing and target audience answers.

title: Add a privacy policy link inside the app
statusNote: Settings > Privacy & data in game/src/ui/screens/settings.js has no policy link, which Play requires.
steps: Add a Privacy policy button in Settings > Privacy & data
Open the hosted URL in the system browser
Add photo/font credits to the About line
Rebuild and test on device
feedback: Play's User Data policy needs the link in Play Console AND in the app.
doneMessage: The app meets Play's in-app privacy policy rule.

title: Move the banner away from the keypad during play
statusNote: ads.js shows the banner during play directly under the glyph keypad, an accidental-click risk.
steps: Add a 16dp+ gap between keypad and banner, or hide it in play
Add optional test device ids to AdMob.initialize
Optionally set maxAdContentRating in initialize
Check layouts on small phones and tablets
feedback: 'Layout encourages accidental clicks' is a top AdMob violation.
Never place ads where a tap meant for the game can land.
doneMessage: Ad placement is now policy-safe, reducing the risk of limited serving or suspension.

title: Enable R8 shrinking and mark the app as a game
statusNote: game/android/app/build.gradle has minifyEnabled false; the manifest lacks android:appCategory=game.
steps: Set minifyEnabled true and shrinkResources true for release
Use proguard-android-optimize.txt; add keep rules if needed
Add android:appCategory="game" to <application>
Test ads, consent, haptics, preferences on a release build
feedback: From Feb 2027 Play wants at least 25% R8 optimization coverage.
Capacitor ships consumer ProGuard rules; plugin crashes mean a missing keep rule.
appCategory=game keeps orientation handling on large screens.
doneMessage: The release build is smaller and ready for Play's 2027 quality thresholds.

title: Create and back up the upload key
statusNote: No keystore or android/keystore.properties exists; the Gradle signing config is ready for one.
steps: keytool -genkeypair -v -keystore alien-sudoku-upload.jks -alias upload -keyalg RSA -keysize 2048 -validity 10000
Save the .jks and both passwords in a password manager
Keep an offline backup copy
Add ANDROID_KEYSTORE_* GitHub secrets or keystore.properties
Never commit the keystore
feedback: Validity must run past 22 Oct 2033; 25+ years is recommended.
Let Play generate the app signing key; this is only the upload key.
A lost upload key can be reset, but it takes days.
doneMessage: Builds can now be signed for upload to Play.

title: Unblock Android release builds
statusNote: dl.google.com is blocked in this workspace (no Android SDK) and GitHub Actions jobs don't start.
steps: Option A: fix Actions billing/spending limit so jobs run
Option B: install Android Studio on your computer
Option C: allow dl.google.com and maven.google.com in this environment
Run one debug build to prove the pipeline works
feedback: Without a working build nothing can reach Play Console.
Public repos get standard Actions runners free.
doneMessage: You have a working way to produce AABs, which unlocks every testing step.

title: Wire real AdMob ids into the production build
statusNote: tools/set-admob-ids.mjs and VITE_ADMOB_ANDROID_* support real ids; none exist yet.
steps: Run set-admob-ids.mjs with the real Android app id
Set VITE_ADMOB_ANDROID_BANNER/INTERSTITIAL/REWARDED secrets
Keep test ids for internal/closed builds if preferred
Check USING_TEST_ADS is false in the production build
feedback: Never click live ads on your own phone; register it as a test device.
A mismatched app id in the manifest crashes the ads SDK at start.
doneMessage: The production build will earn real ad revenue once AdMob approves the app.

title: Build the signed release AAB
statusNote: No AAB can be built until google-build-pipeline and google-upload-key are done.
steps: npm run build && npx cap sync android
./gradlew bundleRelease -PversionCode=N -PversionName=1.0.0
Raise versionCode for every upload
Check the bundle has no unaligned lib/*.so (16 KB)
Check the merged manifest includes AD_ID
feedback: Don't mix local builds (versionCode 1) with CI run numbers.
Updates must support 16 KB pages from 1 Feb 2027; this app has no native code.
doneMessage: You have an uploadable AAB; head to internal testing.

title: Generate icon, feature graphic and screenshots
statusNote: game/tools/store-assets.mjs can render them, but no Play images have been produced yet.
steps: npm run build, then node tools/store-assets.mjs <out>
Icon 512x512 32-bit PNG under 1 MB
Feature graphic 1024x500 JPEG or 24-bit PNG, no alpha
4-8 phone shots 1080x1920 of real gameplay
7-inch and 10-inch tablet shots (e.g. 1200x1920, 1600x2560)
feedback: No test-ad banners, fake reviews or ranking claims in images.
Lead with the puzzle and sci-fi look, not the cutest aliens.
doneMessage: Your listing has every required graphic at the exact sizes Play accepts.

title: Fill in the main store listing
statusNote: Text drafts exist in store-launch/listing/listing.json; support email/URL are still TODO.
steps: Name: Alien Sudoku (30 max)
Short description (80 max) and full description (4000 max)
Append the mobile ads line to the full description
Upload icon, feature graphic, phone and tablet shots
Category Game > Puzzle; add up to 5 tags
Contact: email, website (for app-ads.txt)
feedback: Reword 'cuddly' and 'Baby Blip' to reduce child appeal.
No 'best', '#1', emoji or keyword stuffing.
The website must be the host that serves app-ads.txt.
doneMessage: The store page is complete and ready for review.

title: Answer privacy, ads, access and other declarations
statusNote: No Play app exists yet, so no App content forms are filled.
steps: Privacy policy: paste the hosted URL
App access: all functionality available without restrictions
Ads: Yes, my app contains ads
Government app: No; Financial features: none
Health: none; News app: No
feedback: Misstating ads can get the app suspended.
No sensitive permissions, so no permission forms apply.
doneMessage: The simple declarations are done; on to rating, audience and data safety.

title: Complete the IARC content rating questionnaire
statusNote: Not started; needs the Play app to exist.
steps: Category: Game
Violence, sex, language, drugs, gambling: No
Scary content: Yes, mild cartoon monsters (Gnarly Horde)
User interaction, location sharing, purchases: No
Unrestricted internet: No
Expect about ESRB Everyone, PEGI 3 or 7 (Fear)
feedback: Answer honestly; a wrong rating can be overridden and the app removed.
The typed name stays on the device, so it isn't user interaction.
Redo the questionnaire if you add scarier content.
doneMessage: The game has its official age ratings for every region.

title: Set target audience to 13+ and answer child appeal
statusNote: Not started; PRIVACY.md already says the game is not for under-13s.
steps: Tick 13-15, 16-17 and 18+ only
Answer the 'appeal to children' question honestly
Neutralize the listing first (section 4 of the guide)
Keep AdMob max rating at PG or G
feedback: Ticking any under-13 group brings in the Families policy.
Families needs a neutral age screen and child-directed ad tagging.
Google may add a 'Not designed for children' label.
doneMessage: Your audience is set, which decides which ad rules apply.

title: Complete Data safety and Advertising ID forms
statusNote: Not started; answers are in section 5.6 of google.md.
steps: Collects or shares data: Yes; encrypted in transit: Yes
No account creation; deletion requests: No
Approximate location, App interactions, Diagnostics, Device IDs
Each: collected + shared, required; ads, analytics, fraud
Advertising ID: Yes, same purposes
Check Google's current AdMob data disclosure table
feedback: The typed name never leaves the device, so don't declare it.
Update the form if you add analytics or mediation.
doneMessage: Your privacy labels match the ads SDK, a common rejection reason avoided.

title: Recruit 15-20 Android testers in a Google Group
statusNote: No testers or group exist yet; 12 must stay opted in for 14 days.
steps: Create a Google Group, e.g. alien-sudoku-testers
Invite friends, family, puzzle communities
Collect Gmail addresses of Android users
Explain they must join, opt in and stay 14 days
feedback: Recruit more than 12; people drop out.
Engaged testers make the production application easier.
doneMessage: You have enough testers to start the 14-day clock as soon as a build is approved.

title: Upload to internal testing and test on your phone
statusNote: No AAB exists to upload yet.
steps: Testing > Internal testing > Create release
Accept Play App Signing (Google-generated key)
Upload the AAB; add yourself as tester
Install from the Play link; test consent, ads, back, offline
Read the pre-launch report and fix crashes
feedback: Internal testing doesn't count toward the 12-tester rule.
Test on Android 15 and 16 for edge-to-edge and back gestures.
doneMessage: The first Play build works on a real phone; promote it to closed testing.

title: Run the 14-day closed test with 12+ testers
statusNote: Required for personal accounts created after 13 Nov 2023; not started.
steps: Testing > Closed testing > create track, add the Group
Promote the build; wait for review
Share the opt-in link with testers
Keep 12+ opted in for 14 straight days
Collect feedback; ship 1-2 updates
feedback: Testers who leave early don't count.
Keep notes on feedback for the production application.
doneMessage: The closed test is complete; you can apply for production access.

title: Check US age-verification law duties
statusNote: Texas SB 2420 is enforceable since July 2026; impact on a no-account game is unverified.
steps: Read Play's Age Signals help page
Confirm the IARC rating is accurate
Note: report significant changes in Play Console > Age signals
Decide if Age Signals API is needed (likely not for v1)
feedback: Never use age signal data for ads or analytics.
Re-check before adding purchases or accounts.
doneMessage: You know your US age-law obligations before going public.

title: Apply for production access
statusNote: Unlocks only after the closed test completes.
steps: Dashboard > Apply for production
Describe recruitment, engagement and feedback
Explain what you changed and why it's ready
Submit and wait for the email
feedback: Vague answers get rejected; be specific.
If rejected, fix what Google names and reapply.
doneMessage: Production (and open testing) is unlocked for your account.

title: Release to production with real ads
statusNote: Needs production access and a build with real AdMob ids.
steps: Upload the AAB with real ids and a higher versionCode
Choose countries (consider trader status for EEA/UK)
Use a staged rollout, e.g. 20% then 100%
Optionally turn on Managed publishing
Submit for review
feedback: Make sure the store listing matches the build.
Fix any pre-launch report crashes before submitting.
doneMessage: Alien Sudoku is live on Google Play!

title: Link the AdMob app to the live Play listing
statusNote: AdMob can only link after the app is public on Play.
steps: AdMob > Apps > Alien Sudoku > App settings
Add app store details; search the Play listing
Wait for the app readiness review email
feedback: Ads are limited until the review and app-ads.txt pass.
Closed-test apps can't be found in store search.
doneMessage: AdMob has verified the app, so ads can serve fully.

title: Publish and verify app-ads.txt
statusNote: No developer website or app-ads.txt exists yet.
steps: Copy the line from AdMob > Apps > app-ads.txt
google.com, pub-XXXX, DIRECT, f08c47fec0942fa0
Serve it at https://<website-host>/app-ads.txt
Make sure the Play listing website is that same host
AdMob > app-ads.txt tab > Check for updates
feedback: Must be at the root of the host, not a sub-folder.
Status can take 24 hours or more to update.
doneMessage: Advertisers can verify your inventory, which lifts limited serving.

title: Add tax info, bank details and verify the PIN
statusNote: No AdMob payments profile or tax info yet.

steps: AdMob > Payments > Manage settings
Add US tax info (W-9, individual)
Add a bank account for EFT
Enter the mailed PIN when it arrives (within 4 months)
feedback: Payments go out around the 21st once over $100.
Tax info must be in by the 20th to be paid that month.
doneMessage: Your ad earnings can be paid out each month.

title: Monitor vitals, policy and 2027 deadlines
statusNote: Nothing is live yet to monitor.
steps: Check Android vitals: crashes, ANRs, memory
Check Play policy inbox and AdMob policy center
Reply to reviews
Calendar: 1 Feb 2027 trader + 16 KB; Feb 2027 memory/DEX
feedback: Crash rate above 1.09% hurts visibility.
Respond to policy emails before the deadline.
doneMessage: You'll catch problems before they cost installs or ad revenue.

title: Plan the 2027 ads SDK and target API upgrade
statusNote: @capacitor-community/admob 8.3 uses legacy ads SDK 25.4.x, deprecated 30 Jun 2027.
steps: Track the plugin's Next-Gen SDK support
Upgrade before 30 Jun 2027 (sunset 30 Jun 2028)
Bump targetSdk when Play announces the 2027 level
Re-run consent and ad tests after upgrading
feedback: After sunset, ads may stop serving entirely.
Android 17 target removes the large-screen opt-out.
doneMessage: Ads and API levels stay current, so revenue doesn't stop in 2028.

title: Optional: publish on Samsung Galaxy Store
statusNote: No Samsung seller account; optional after Play launch.
steps: Create a Samsung account and Seller Portal registration
Request commercial seller status (needed even for free apps)
Download the Play-signed universal APK from App bundle explorer
Import the listing from Play; upload the APK
Or register your own signing key in Play's developer verification page
feedback: Galaxy Store enforces Android developer verification.
AdMob works on Samsung phones (they have Google Play services).
doneMessage: Samsung phone owners can find the game in their default store too.

title: Skip Amazon Appstore and Huawei AppGallery for now
statusNote: Amazon closed its Android phone store on 20 Aug 2025; Huawei phones lack Google ads services.
steps: Note Amazon only serves Fire tablets/TV now
Note HUAWEI Ads doesn't accept individuals
Revisit only if you add another ad network
feedback: AdMob depends on Google Play services, missing on Fire and new Huawei devices.
